opex.note: Building chips, modems and AI platforms; down 1% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative

footerNote: Qualcomm guided Q4 FY25 revenue to $10.3B–$11.1B and non-GAAP EPS to $2.75–$2.95.
oneTimers: Operating expenses include $85M of losses from revaluing deferred compensation plan liabilities, roughly offset by $84M of gains on the related plan assets inside investment income — the two nearly cancel out.
The tax line includes a $117M foreign currency gain on a refund claim for Korean withholding taxes paid in prior years, partly offset by a $105M charge for uncertain tax benefits from prior years.
Non-GAAP results also exclude $65M of acquisition-related charges and a $13M impairment loss on investments.
otherDetail: Investment and other income of $358M, less $168M of interest expense, makes up the $190M outside operations.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 29, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Automotive and IoT combined grew 23% YoY to $2.67B — Automotive set a record at $984M (+21%) and IoT rose 24% to $1.68B — as Qualcomm's push beyond phones kept paying off.
takeaways.title: Diversification is working

takeaways.text: Handset chips still brought in the most money: $6.33B, up 7% YoY and 61% of total revenue, inside QCT's $8.99B (+11%).
takeaways.title: Handsets still the engine

takeaways.text: Qualcomm returned $3.8B to shareholders in the quarter — $2.8B of buybacks (19 million shares) plus $967M of dividends — and guided Q4 FY25 revenue to $10.3B–$11.1B.
takeaways.title: Cash back to shareholders

verdict: Qualcomm grew revenue 10% to $10.4B as its car and connected-device chips hit records, while the phone chips that still pay most of the bills grew 7%.
